models.purpose: Convert prior Olympic outcomes into four athlete or team capability features for the medal classifiers.
models.summary: For each athlete or consolidated team, the paper accumulates prior medal and gold indicators, takes a lagged cumulative best ordinal result, and divides prior ordinal-score mass by prior appearances. Every definition uses shift(1) to exclude the current row.

Indicator that athlete or team i won gold at Games s.

Number of appearances for i before cutoff Games t.
Cumulative MedalBinary total before Games t.
Cumulative GoldBinary total before Games t.
Best ordinal result before Games t.
Mean prior ordinal result before Games t.

governing_equations.label: prose definition 1
governing_equations.source_expression: PastTotalMedals is calculated by summing MedalBinary values and applying shift(1) to exclude the current year.
governing_equations.purpose: Count prior medal-winning appearances without the current row.

governing_equations.label: prose definition 2
governing_equations.source_expression: PastGoldMedals is derived by summing GoldBinary values and applying shift(1).
governing_equations.purpose: Count prior gold-winning appearances.

governing_equations.label: prose definition 3
governing_equations.source_expression: PastBestResult is the cumulative maximum of the 3/2/1/0 score, shifted once.
governing_equations.purpose: Retain the best result observed before the prediction cutoff.

governing_equations.label: prose definition 4
governing_equations.source_expression: PastWeightedRatio is cumulative previous score divided by the number of previous participations, using shift(1).
governing_equations.purpose: Measure average prior ordinal performance.

equation_status.reason: Four prose definitions on PDF page 8 were visually checked and normalized without adding a new statistical claim.

objectives: Represent experience, gold history, peak performance, and average ordinal performance using only prior rows.
constraints: Rows must be ordered within athlete or consolidated team before shift(1).
The current Games must not enter any cumulative feature.

details: Athletes with no prior appearance require an explicit zero or missing-value convention.
PBR lies in 0-3 and PWR requires a nonzero prior-appearance denominator.
These are historical summaries rather than a dynamic equilibrium model.

parameter_estimation.method: The four features are deterministic transforms; no fitted parameter is stated.

steps: Group rows by athlete or consolidated team.
Order rows by Olympic year.
Compute cumulative medal, gold, maximum-result, and score totals.
Apply shift(1) and divide the score total by prior appearances.
software: pandas operations are implied by shift(1), but code is not supplied.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not applicable to deterministic cumulative transforms.

assumptions: Historical athlete identity is reconciled across Games.
The 3/2/1/0 score is treated as an informative numeric ordering.
A one-row shift is sufficient to enforce the cutoff after correct grouping and sorting.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Definitions are executable, but the paper does not show the entity keys, same-Games row handling, zero-history convention, or tests proving that shift(1) prevents within-Games leakage.

validation_refs: Figure 4 shows two athlete radar profiles but no feature-level predictive ablation.
The later random-fold diagnostics test the classifier, not cutoff correctness.
models.computational_cost: Linear in athlete-event rows after grouping and year ordering; exact grouping cost and row count are omitted.
strengths: Makes the temporal cutoff explicit through lagging.
Separates experience, gold history, peak, and average performance.
limitations: The ordinal result scale is treated as cardinal.
Multiple rows in one Games can leak unless grouping and ordering are exact.
missing_details: Treatment of duplicate same-year event rows.

Random-forest or fallback probability of gold.

governing_equations.source_expression: Call predict_proba to obtain Prob_Gold from the sport-specific gold model or fallback rate.
governing_equations.purpose: Define the gold probability consumed by allocation.

objectives: Classify medal and gold outcomes separately within each sport.
Provide athlete-level probabilities for deterministic and stochastic medal allocation.
constraints: Training and 2028 feature columns must match.
Sparse or one-class sports use the stated fallback instead of a fitted forest.

Both probability outputs lie in 0-1; fallback behavior activates below five entries or with one class.
Static supervised classifiers have no equilibrium condition.

2024 participants and events represent 2028.
Random row splits are suitable for a future-Games forecast.

models.section: 3.1.6-3.1.7 Medal Distribution and Monte Carlo Simulation
models.purpose: Translate athlete probabilities into country gold and total-medal forecasts and intervals.
models.summary: The point procedure assigns gold to the maximum Prob_Gold athlete and the remaining two medal slots to the highest Prob_Medal athletes. governing_equations.purpose: Normalize the relevant probability over entrants still eligible for a slot.

governing_equations.source_expression: Summarize gold medals for each country from all event drawing results.
governing_equations.purpose: Aggregate simulated event gold awards to the requested country gold total.

equation_status.reason: The allocation and aggregation equations are faithful normalizations of the visually checked page 10-11 procedure.

objectives: Estimate conditional country medal-count distributions and empirical intervals.
constraints: Within each event, selected entrants are removed before later draws.
The described rule assigns one gold and two other medal slots per event.
All country totals must equal the allocated event slots after team handling.

details: Every simulation starts from the same fixed 2028 roster and fitted probabilities.
Drawing stops after three distinct winners or when no positive weight remains.
Independent repeated draws do not seek an equilibrium.

parameter_estimation.method: Probabilities are inherited from the classifiers; M is chosen as 1000 for the reported Task 1 run, with 5000 or 10000 mentioned as alternatives.

steps: For every event, draw one gold winner with Prob_Gold.
Remove the selected entrant.
Draw two further medalists with normalized Prob_Medal without replacement.
Aggregate gold and total medals by NOC.
Repeat M times and compute empirical summaries and quantiles.
software: Monte Carlo pseudocode is described, but executable code and random seeds are absent.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: No Monte Carlo error target or quantile-stability diagnostic is reported; only example repeat counts are given.

assumptions: Fitted probabilities remain fixed across repetitions.
The fixed roster and event program are known.
A common three-winner rule is adequate across sports and team events.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The simulation is operationally reconstructable, but team awards, ties, double-bronze sports, quotas, event-specific rules, and probability calibration are not reconciled.

validation_refs: Figure 5 shows point country forecasts.
Figure 6 and Table 1 show leading-country interval outputs.
Figure 7 shows input-probability diagnostics rather than country-total backtests.
models.computational_cost: Approximately linear in simulations times events times entrants used in weighted draws; actual entrant count, runtime, and seed policy are omitted.
strengths: Enforces no repeat winner within an event draw.
Connects entrant probabilities to official NOC totals and intervals.
limitations: Intervals vary only outcome draws conditional on fixed inputs and therefore omit roster, program, parameter, calibration, and structural uncertainty.
A universal award rule does not match every Olympic sport.
missing_details: Monte Carlo convergence and all-country intervals.

models.section: 3.3.3-3.3.5 Event Count Analyses for USA Swimming and China Table Tennis
models.purpose: Relate athlete-row medal totals to the number of events in a sport and compare USA swimming with China table tennis.
models.summary: Separate Poisson regressions use sport-year medal totals as outcomes and event count as the predictor. USA swimming is reported first with beta1 0.0517, then with a conflicting 0.1912 sensitivity fit; China table tennis reports beta1 0.1273 with p=0.59. The paper exponentiates beta1, plots predictions, defines elasticity beta1 times event count, and performs leave-one-year-out refits.
